reuse.why: getNextDate drops the existing applyWeekendRule/getDateWithSkippedWeekend and re-implements weekend shifting inline with holidays, while getDatesInRange, getUpcomingDates and schedule-template keep using applyWeekendRule without holidays, so the shared helper is no longer the single weekend rule.

duplication.why: The daily skip loop is written twice in getNextDate (forward and reverse), the daily weekend skip is written again in getDatesInRange, and the before/after shifting loop duplicates getDateWithSkippedWeekend.

placement.why: getDatesInRange sits sensibly next to getUpcomingDates in server/schedules/app.ts, but the daily-skip and holiday rules are embedded in getNextDate's body instead of in the shared weekend-rule functions of shared/schedules.ts.

scope.why: Edits serve the four steps, though holidays are only wired into getNextDate, leaving other date paths unchanged.

maintainability.why: The weekend/holiday rule now exists in three divergent forms (inline loops in getNextDate, a daily special case in getDatesInRange, and the untouched applyWeekendRule), with magic attempt bounds and an empty if-branch, which invites drift.

bypasses_abstraction.where: shared/schedules.ts getNextDate replaces applyWeekendRule with an inline shift loop; server/schedules/app.ts getDatesInRange handles daily weekends itself and passes skipWeekend:false to applyWeekendRule for daily.

disguised_duplication.where: getNextDate's direction loop (weekendSolve 'before' ? -1 : 1, step until not weekend/holiday) is a reshaped copy of getDateWithSkippedWeekend; the forward and reverse daily-skip loops are mirrored copies of each other.

abstraction_drift.where: applyWeekendRule gains no holidays/daily support; instead getNextDate adds an isDaily branch and its own shifting loop and getDatesInRange adds a daily ternary (skipWeekend: frequency !== 'daily' && ...) plus its own weekend filter, both bypassing the shared helper.
